source_text: Inter te igitur et Manichaeum prosatorem sensuum tuorum, video per profectum eruditionis tuae magnam factam esse distantiam. Ille enim licet duos induxisset auctores, tamen spem salutis ex ea reliquit parte, qua dixit bonum Deum esse alienissimum ab iniquitate, et a crudelitate; tu vero unum bonum quidem Deum, sed eumdem malorum conditorem loquens, ut reverentiam divinitatis, ita spem salutis funditus sustulisti.
pass_a_gloss: Between you therefore and the Manichaean, progenitor of your senses, I see a great distance has been made through the progress of your learning. For he although he had brought in two authors, nevertheless left a hope of salvation from that part, by which he said that the good God is most alien from iniquity, and from cruelty; but you speaking one God indeed good, but the same the founder of evils, as the reverence of divinity, so the hope of salvation you have taken away from the foundations.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS conditor; Blaise God as maker from nothing

pass_b_english: I therefore see a great distance produced by the progress of your learning between you and Mani, the progenitor of your ideas. Although he introduced two authors, he left hope of salvation on the side on which he said that the good God was utterly removed from injustice and cruelty. You, however, by speaking of one good God who is also the Creator of evil people, have utterly abolished both reverence for divinity and hope of salvation.

choices.why: Scripture's destruction of iniquitas is the Law's purpose; keep moral injustice.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
